mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and increases the present value of future cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (25th percentile), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a further rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE rising >0.2pp) signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when UNRATE rises >0.2pp, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS growth < 0.1% and UNRATE > 0.2pp rise) fails to predict negative returns in >50% of cases over 20 days, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand and economic activity, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods when HOUST is above the 75th percentile, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 1300 (thousands of units) signals weak consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods when HOUST < 1300, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of industrial contraction (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO < 100, 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakness in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST < 1300 and RSAFS < 700,000) fails to predict negative returns in >50% of cases over 5 days, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
